scope: PB32Add only, within existing RTE32 normal-sum modules; PB32Subtract/product-residual calls reach the same guarded addition. All original integer bodies and every other primitive remain text-identical. No production adoption, driver-control change or renderer repetition.
native_admission: Both original raw inputs are normal binary32, absolute value <= 2^124; output is finite. Single NoContraction OpFAdd under RTE32. Any nonzero native result is the original correctly rounded result. If native result is zero, exact opposite words canonically return +0; every other case uses the original integer fallback. Inputs containing zero, subnormal, infinity or NaN and large finite inputs use the original path.
underflow_reason: All finite binary32 values are multiples of 2^-149. A nonzero subnormal sum/difference of normal inputs is exactly representable. The only allowed value loss is flushing that result to zero, which the guard detects; bit-preserving operations cannot flush returned subnormal bits.
domain_restriction_reason: Bounded inputs keep native results finite, avoiding a new SignedZeroInfNanPreserve requirement; integer paths retain every exceptional/overflow case.
distinction: Existing RetainedSum32 requires both operands on the 2^-126 lattice via its 2^-103 lower domain. This changes the scalar addition primitive with exact post-operation underflow detection, rather than changing an earlier rejected launch, divide estimate, sum absorption, cancellation-only or upward-add guard.
